clue.text: Object when odd little lad withdraws

indicators.note: to withdraw is to draw back, so the two pieces together are read from the back

parts.note: odd means strange, which is rum in British slang
Ed is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: A complaint raised when a strange small boy backs out of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' is the verb, not a thing. 'withdraws' (draws back) turns RUMED, the run of odd plus little lad, backwards as one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, so it is a verb synonym of object.

clue.text: Supports raffle initially, despite snags

indicators.note: initially says the raffle comes at the start, before the supports

parts.note: a raffle is a prize draw
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone supports the raffle at first although it has problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawbacks are disadvantages or problems, the same sense as snags.

clue.text: Friend harbours revolutionary carrying knife

indicators.note: harbours means shelters within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a mate is a friend
Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A pal is hiding an armed rebel who carries a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used for cutting vegetation.

clue.text: About a thousand pages? No, just half

definitions.text: About a thousand pages? No, just half

parts.words: About a thousand pages? No, just half
parts.note: reads as a stack of five hundred sheets, printed on both sides, giving a thousand pages, though the sheet count is half that

explanation.surface: A reader estimates the length of a long book and is corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard bundle of five hundred sheets of paper.

clue.text: Lure a girl out? That's irregular

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Coaxing a girl outside is unconventional behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LUREAGIRL. 'Irregular' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun: a fighter outside a regular army.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular is a soldier not in a regular army, which describes a partisan fighter of a small band.

clue.text: Sadly dire prospects for fellowship

indicators.note: sadly suggests things are in a sorry state, so the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Gloomy outlook ahead for a group of companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit de corps is the feeling of comradeship and loyalty within a group.

clue.text: Animals retreating into long grass

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the animals' word is read backwards

parts.note: deer are animals, the plural matching

explanation.surface: Creatures backing away into tall vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass-like plant growing near water.

clue.text: Boy admitted into no more classes

indicators.note: admitted into means let inside, so the boy goes inside the other piece

parts.note: less means not more
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is no longer allowed into school lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons are teaching sessions, the same as classes.

clue.text: Accessory needed by fellow on active duty

indicators.note: on says the fellow is added next to the abbreviation for active duty

parts.note: AD is a standard abbreviation for active duty
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Equipment a soldier needs when serving.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra item attached to a product, which is an accessory.

clue.text: Soldiers return with brace that's light

indicators.note: return means the soldiers' letters come back the other way

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a common crossword source of soldiers
a brace that holds things together is a clamp

explanation.surface: Troops come back carrying a support that seems to have little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns RA into AR. 'Light' looks like an adjective meaning not heavy; it is the noun, a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp is an electric lamp giving a very bright light, so it is a kind of light source.

clue.text: Feign disinterest when drama's in short supply

parts.note: a drama is a play
scarce things are hard to get

explanation.surface: Pretending not to care at a time when theatre tickets are scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: To act unavailable is to pretend lack of interest to seem more desirable.

clue.text: Decreased by media boss

parts.note: the press means the news media collectively
ED is short for editor, the boss of a paper

explanation.surface: Something was reduced in size by a newspaper chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decreased' reads as smaller, but is de-creased: flattened by pressing, like an ironed shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something de-creased has had its creases removed by ironing, a punning split of the word.

clue.text: Reared by British Labourite

parts.note: a left-wing Labour Party supporter may be called a red

explanation.surface: A child brought up by a British Labour supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means brought up, raised or nurtured, so it fits as a past participle synonym.

clue.text: Custom-made outfit

definitions.meaning: a custom is a regular practice or routine
a riding costume or a nun's garment is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: Clothing tailored specially for the buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Custom-made' looks like one word meaning tailored; split it, and 'made' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is both a settled practice one follows and a distinctive garment such as a monk's robe.

clue.text: To work at home is murder

parts.note: to do is to work or perform
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Working from home is torture, one complains.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone in is an idiom for killing them.

clue.text: Nut needed to start an engine

definitions.meaning: a nut is an eccentric person
to turn an engine over by hand with a handle

explanation.surface: A small fastener required to get a motor going.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is both an eccentric person and, as a verb, to turn a starting handle.

clue.text: Group of note appears in autumn, and is French

parts.note: Oct, October, is an autumn month
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A notable band plays in autumn, and it is a French one.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a musical ensemble of eight players.

clue.text: Tidy up after card-players

parts.note: reads as gathering up the packs left on the table once a game of cards ends

explanation.surface: Putting things away once the bridge party has gone home.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means get ready for action, literally clearing a ship's decks; here it is read as removing decks of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means remove clutter in preparation, which is tidying up.

clue.text: Black dog that enjoys the high life

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dark-coated hound with a taste for luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy traveller who flies around fashionable places lives a glamorous life.

clue.text: Withheld levy when job was assigned elsewhere

definitions.meaning: opted out of paying a contribution, as in leaving the state pension scheme
work was outsourced to another firm

explanation.surface: Tax went unpaid when the work was handed to another company.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain one could be excused part of the National Insurance levy by opting out of the state earnings-related pension.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both opting out of a scheme's payments and giving work to an outside supplier.

clue.text: Farewell toast

definitions.meaning: a word said when drinking to someone's health

explanation.surface: A drink raised to say goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: This British expression is both an informal goodbye and, dated, a drinking salutation like cheers.

clue.text: Fruit from Ohio mountains

parts.note: O is the postal-style abbreviation for Ohio
ranges are chains of mountains

explanation.surface: Produce shipped from the hills of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: These are citrus fruits.

clue.text: A sanctum in the Yemen

parts.note: a sanctum is a private room or den

explanation.surface: A private retreat somewhere in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: A woman's remains

parts.note: a woman is she, and woman's read as woman is gives she's

explanation.surface: A dead woman's mortal remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman's' must be read as 'woman is', giving SHE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are what is left after cremation, a person's remains.

clue.text: The leading performer, king, is completely unadorned

parts.note: the star of a show is its leading performer
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The headliner playing a monarch appears without any finery.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark means bare and plain, as in stark naked, with nothing added.

clue.text: Get on with a paying passenger

definitions.meaning: to get on is to manage or do
a taxi driver's customer is called a ...

explanation.surface: Getting along well with a customer in the cab.
explanation.definitionFit: To fare is to progress or manage, and a fare is also a passenger who pays for the ride.

clue.text: Know the way to Mayfair

parts.note: Mayfair is in London's W1 postal district, the 1 read as the letter I
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Directions for finding a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is a wealthy district in central London. Wist is an archaic verb meaning know.
explanation.definitionFit: Wist is an old form of wit, an archaic verb meaning to be aware of.

clue.text: Defeat utterly, then defect

definitions.meaning: an old verb sense: to break, ruin or render void

explanation.surface: Someone is thrashed and then deserts to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defect' looks like the verb to desert; it is the noun, a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old verb it meant to crack or nullify, and as a noun it is a blemish or imperfection.

clue.text: What fiance may flaunt to get fish

parts.note: an engaged man may show off the ring he gave to his bride-to-be
the item shown off is a ring, the engagement token

explanation.surface: A newly engaged man proudly showing off before going fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The engagement ring belongs to her, the fiancee, so the man flaunts her ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A herring is a silvery food fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Sarah and I bought a chestnut

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the name Sarah
got means acquired, as in I got it at the market

explanation.surface: Two people went shopping and came home with a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The saligot is the water chestnut, the edible nut of an aquatic plant.

clue.text: Essential clothing items for baseball player

parts.note: shorts are a basic piece of clothing
a top is a basic upper garment

explanation.surface: A list of the kit every ballplayer must wear.
explanation.walkthrough: A shortstop is the fielder placed between second and third base.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortstop is a fielding position in baseball, so it names one kind of player.

clue.text: Way Rex employed to get more sage

parts.note: wise is an old word for manner or way, as in in no wise
R stands for Rex, Latin for king, as in the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A path that a king took to gain wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' is a link word; WISE in the sense 'way' survives in 'in this wise' and 'otherwise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiser is the comparative of a word meaning sensible, so it equals more sage.
